_doc: The SA-02m-web-build quality-tools registry (PROTOCOL.md `## Quality tools`). The one home for 'what does GREEN mean for this web project'. Each row is a self-contained check the runner (`.ai-dev/quality/run.mjs <beat>`) executes wholesale for its beat. The Builder runs every `build`-beat tool on completion and hands back only when they pass; the Reviewer confirms the `review`-beat tools ran and reads their output; `ship`-beat tools run before the merge stamp. Adding or changing a tool = a row here + (optionally) its native config beside this file — never a runner edit.

_row_shape.checks: one plain line: what this tool catches
_row_shape.config: path to its native config beside this file, or null if none
_row_shape.run: the command to run it (from the project root — the runner's cwd)
_row_shape.covers: optional array of path prefixes/globs; run.mjs --touched runs a row only when the diff touches a covered path (rows without covers always run)
_row_shape.init: one line: how to install/enable it

tools.checks: Syntax errors in every hand-written frontend script under static/js/ (recursive: the top-level bundles, app/*.js from the F10 decomposition, and any module directory added later — mqtt/, flasher/, ...) — a broken script bricks the whole UI since there is no build step. MODULE-AWARE: a file with a line-leading `import`/`export` is checked via `node --input-type=module --check < file` because plain `node --check` exits 0 on a broken .js ES module (Node 20/24 module-detection — docs/decisions/es-modules.md П1); classic scripts keep `node --check`. Non-vacuous: zero files swept = FAIL; the module/classic split is pinned by scripts/dev/test-js-syntax-gate.sh (row js-syntax-gate).
tools.init: Node 18+ + bash

tools.checks: Non-vacuity of the js-syntax row (scripts/dev/test-js-syntax-gate.sh): re-proves on the local Node that `node --check` passes a broken .js module, then asserts the shipped gate FAILS a broken module and a broken classic script, PASSES valid ones, does not misread the bundles' `exportHistory()`/`exported_at:` lines or a dynamic `import()` as module syntax (a non-strict classic body must not be parsed as a module), fails a missing file, and sweeps a non-empty tree. Without it the module branch of the gate could silently regress to the pre-fix vacuous pass the day the first ES module lands.
tools.init: bash + Node 18+ (no other deps) — run on demand: bash scripts/dev/test-js-syntax-gate.sh

tools.checks: Bash syntax errors in every CGI endpoint and shared lib — a broken CGI returns 500 with no client-side trace.
tools.run: bash -c 'set -e; for f in www/network_config/cgi-bin/*.cgi www/network_config/cgi-bin/lib_*.sh; do bash -n "$f"; done'
tools.init: bash (present everywhere the project builds)

tools.checks: Syntax errors in every on-device Python service under opt/ (the Modbus-MQTT bridge, snapshot/scan/monitor helpers, the flasher) — a broken script fails only at systemd start on the device, with no build step to catch it.
tools.run: bash -c 'for p in python3 python py; do if "$p" -c "import sys"; then exec "$p" -m compileall -q opt/; fi; done; echo py-syntax: no working python interpreter; exit 1'
tools.init: Python 3.10+ as python3, python, or py — same interpreter picker as version-consistency (Windows ships a non-functional python3 Store stub)

tools.checks: Bridge unit tests (opt/sa02m-modbus-mqtt/tests — FMB event manager generalization, MR-02m dispatch golden values, DTV event ranges/scaling) — a regression in the event path passes py-syntax but fails here.
tools.run: bash -c 'for p in python3 python py; do if "$p" -c "import sys"; then exec "$p" -m unittest discover -s opt/sa02m-modbus-mqtt/tests -q; fi; done; echo py-unit: no working python interpreter; exit 1'
tools.init: Python 3.10+ (stdlib unittest, no extra deps) — same interpreter picker as py-syntax

tools.checks: Cloud-agent stdlib unit tests (opt/sa02m-cloud-agent/tests, unittest-style test_render*.py). Despite the pattern name this row now covers the whole agent seam: frpc.toml rendering + the device-side local-port allow-list (drops :22/:1883, keeps :80/:9999) + pinned transport TLS (A5 defense-in-depth), per-device identity metadatas emission and 0600 credential storage, the heartbeat send-only guarantee (threat-model F1), and revocation stand-down/recovery. The test_render*.py pattern deliberately excludes the pytest-style test_agent.py (pytest is not a device/CI dep) — widening it to test_*.py would fail the gate on the missing import.
tools.run: bash -c 'for p in python3 python py; do if "$p" -c "import sys"; then exec "$p" -m unittest discover -s opt/sa02m-cloud-agent/tests -p "test_render*.py" -q; fi; done; echo py-unit-cloud: no working python interpreter; exit 1'
tools.init: Python 3.10+ (stdlib unittest, no extra deps) — same interpreter picker as py-unit

tools.checks: Flasher unit tests (opt/sa02m-flasher/tests, stdlib unittest) — firmware formats/repo, scan persist, MPLC port lease, application-line profiles, and the by-address bootloader reg-290 signature preflight (1.0.5.17). A regression in the flash routing/signature path passes py-syntax but fails here. Uses -t opt/sa02m-flasher so the sa02m_flasher package imports from any cwd.
tools.run: bash -c 'for p in python3 python py; do if "$p" -c "import sys"; then exec "$p" -m unittest discover -s opt/sa02m-flasher/tests -t opt/sa02m-flasher -q; fi; done; echo py-unit-flasher: no working python interpreter; exit 1'
tools.init: Python 3.10+ (stdlib unittest, no extra deps) — same interpreter picker as py-unit

tools.checks: Alice controller unit tests (opt/sa02m-alice/tests, stdlib unittest) — converters, device registry, state-sender rate limits, and honest offline/gateway-down API (no fake pairing success).
tools.run: bash -c 'for p in python3 python py; do if "$p" -c "import sys"; then exec "$p" -m unittest discover -s opt/sa02m-alice/tests -t opt/sa02m-alice -q; fi; done; echo py-unit-alice: no working python interpreter; exit 1'
tools.init: Python 3.10+ (stdlib unittest, no extra deps) — same interpreter picker as py-unit

tools.checks: MPLC4 project-deploy zip validator/extractor tests (opt/sa02m-mplc/tests, stdlib unittest) — the security net for the «Обновление проекта MPLC» upload surface: zip-slip/traversal rejection, symlink-member rejection, the closed 4-member cfg/ allow-list, per-entry/total size caps (anti zip-bomb), ProjInfo.json sanity, fixed-basename extraction a hostile entry name cannot redirect, and binary-safe multipart parsing. A regression that reopens a code-escape path passes py-syntax but fails here.
tools.run: bash -c 'for p in python3 python py; do if "$p" -c "import sys"; then exec "$p" -m unittest discover -s opt/sa02m-mplc/tests -t opt/sa02m-mplc -q; fi; done; echo py-unit-mplc: no working python interpreter; exit 1'
tools.init: Python 3.10+ (stdlib unittest, no extra deps) — same interpreter picker as py-unit

tools.checks: Static gate for docs/contracts/mplc-project-deploy.md: the CGI checks auth AND requires CSRF before the sudo helper launch (mutation), the deploy target is the hard-coded MPLC_CFG_DIR=/opt/mplc4/server/cfg (never request-derived — zip-slip floor) with a literal SVC_ID=mplc4, the zip is handled in Python zipfile with the closed 4-member cfg/ allow-list + traversal/symlink rejection, the sudoers grant is exactly one pinned helper path, and the reversible-deploy floors survive: backup precedes the rm of the live project, restore() runs on failure, success is gated on the RT 'load successful' signal (LoadConfig() error -> E_VERIFY, no false green), a backup retention cap, timeouts on stop/start/verify, and the flasher port-lease refusal.
tools.init: bash + grep (present everywhere the project builds)

tools.checks: Static gate for docs/contracts/ethernet-iface-naming.md: the legacy-name ledger (only the compat layer, the rename script and the installer migration may name end0/end1 — non-vacuous both ways), the installer still installing AND enabling sa02m-iface-canonical.service, the F6 guard (no `echo -e` in apply.cgi and conf writes only through the two known writers), the §5.4 rm-helper pins (no raw `sudo rm` in apply.cgi; the pinned sa02m-conf-rm.sh sudoers grant present), and the contract §1.0/§7 ordering pins: the unit ordered Before=networking.service, After=+Wants= systemd-udevd + systemd-udev-trigger (else the boot-0 pre-udevd no-op returns), NO Wants=systemd-udev-settle (else the 120 s whole-queue stall returns), fix-eth@.service After=networking.service (else the double-ifup 'File exists' race returns), the rename script still gating canonicalize_pair on udev_initialized (else the boot-0 class returns silently), and 02-network.sh writing `source /etc/network/interfaces.d/*.conf` with no unfiltered `*` line (else <conf>.sa02m-bak backups go live: duplicate stanza -> 'File exists' -> networking FAILED, §1.0 mechanism 3).
tools.init: bash + grep (present everywhere the project builds)

tools.checks: Static gate for docs/contracts/kernel-conditional-services.md: the opcua gateway port default agrees between etc/sa02m-mqtt-opcua.conf and BOTH py defaults and is not 4840 (CODESYS's own OPC UA server owns 4840 — a regression re-creates the EADDRINUSE crash-loop), sa02m-grat-arp@.service stays Type=simple (a oneshot regression re-blocks multi-user.target ~29 s), the kernel-service guard script + unit + docker ExecCondition drop-in exist and 01-system.sh installs/enables them and runs apply-policy, 08-codesys.sh carries no unconditional enable/start of codesyscontrol (install-only policy), service-ctl cmd_start/codesys_install carry no codesys_rc_enable (start = runtime only), the boot-hold pins: sa02m-modem-dhcp@.service stays event-driven (no [Install] — a statically enabled instance holds multi-user ~90 s on an absent modem) with the 99-modem.rules start line and the 01-system.sh stale-symlink cleanup in place, and sa02m-mqtt-opcua.py sends exactly one sd_notify("READY=1") at the top of main() BEFORE `gw = OpcuaGateway(cfg)` (early READY decouples the OPC UA address-space build — ~9 s in OpcuaServer() construction inside __init__, ~17 s total — from multi-user.target; moving it into/after construction reintroduces the boot hold, contract §5.1). Non-vacuous: a missing file or an empty extraction FAILS.
tools.init: bash + grep (present everywhere the project builds)

tools.checks: Static gate for the hardware watchdog policy homed in etc/systemd/sa02m-watchdog.conf. Cap pin (open-world): it SWEEPS etc/ scripts/ tools/ opt/ www/ install.sh, so a brand-new writer is judged too, not just the enumerated copies — every RuntimeWatchdogSec/RebootWatchdogSec/ShutdownWatchdogSec value parses to <=16s (the sun4i-wdt cap on the A40i) or is an explicit disable, with durations NORMALISED first: a naive compare reads the original defect's `2min` as 2, and the spaced form `2 min` (valid per systemd.time(7)) must reach the parser intact rather than truncating to `2`. docs/ and .ai-dev/ are deliberately NOT swept — BUGLOG quotes the historical bad values as the defects it records. Plus: RuntimeWatchdogSec=15s and RebootWatchdogSec=0 in every copy that carries the values literally; no active ShutdownWatchdogSec= (deprecated pre-v243 alias); the firstboot-overlay copy byte-identical to the policy home; and 01-system.sh installing the drop-in from $ETC_REPO with no inline heredoc (it used to ship its own competing 10s/4min values to the same path). Plus the second mechanism of the same defect class, invisible to the directive pins: direct sysfs writes to /sys/class/watchdog/*/timeout (the feeder etc/sa02m-watchdog-feed.sh and its heredoc twin in tools/imaging/ssh-flash-safe.sh used to `echo 30 >` it against a 16s driver, the rejection swallowed by `|| true`) must be CLAMPED — no numeric literal above the cap, and every file writing the path also reads max_timeout on an uncommented line, so a file cannot satisfy the pin by naming the clamp in prose. A FAIL means a device would get a timeout systemd or the driver rejects, or a copy silently diverged from the policy home. Non-vacuous both ways: a missing enumerated file, a dead sweep, an empty extraction, or fewer than the two expected sysfs write sites FAILS. Deliberate non-flags: `=0` disables, commented-out lines (the imaging comment-out sed idiom), and READS of the sysfs timeout (max_timeout is the clamp's input).
tools.init: bash + grep (present everywhere the project builds)

tools.checks: Static gate for the RTC time-frame convention (home: the comment block at the DS3231 load in etc/sa02m-pre-start.sh) — the battery-backed chip holds UTC, so every conversion between system time and chip time must NAME utc rather than inherit it from /etc/adjtime, a file nothing in this repo writes and that timedatectl set-local-rtc / a different base image / a restored backup can flip. The class hit twice in two releases: the pre-start read half was fixed first, then lib_rtc.sh was found still writing the chip with local `date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S'` — with sa02m-rtc-sync.timer firing every 30 min and the I2C path active whenever /dev/rtc1 is absent, the clock moved one timezone per write and the skew reached system time at the next boot. Pins: every hwclock chip access carries --utc (open-world over etc/ scripts/ tools/ opt/ www/ install.sh, resolved THROUGH the variable each file binds the binary to — not one shipped call site spells `hwclock` on the invocation line, so a literal grep would pass vacuously); every write_*_i2c_datetime function builds its timestamp with date -u (swept by DEFINITION, so a new chip writer in a new file is judged); every `date -s` fed by a chip-read value carries -u; nothing switches the frame to local (set-local-rtc / adjtime LOCAL); and no chip-vs-system comparison string-compares instead of computing an epoch — hwclock --show prints LOCAL time with a +03:00 offset, and a parser dropping that offset already reported a false 3-hour skew during this very fix. Non-vacuous: a missing enumerated file, fewer than 6 resolved hwclock accesses, a known caller contributing zero, fewer than 2 I2C write functions, a write function with no extractable timestamp, or no chip-sourced `date -s` FAILS rather than passing on zero matches. Deliberate non-flags: fake-hwclock (a timestamp file, no frame — masked before matching), commented-out lines, docs/ and .ai-dev/ (CHANGELOG/BUGLOG quote the bad form as the defect they record), apply.cgi's `date -s` on the operator-supplied wall-clock value (local by contract), year-plausibility tests against a constant, and the sudoers path allow-list naming /sbin/hwclock. --localtime is NOT accepted as an explicit frame: the repo declares one convention.
tools.init: bash + grep + awk (present everywhere the project builds)

tools.checks: Functional regression for apply.cgi's /etc/network/interfaces.d foreign-stanza merge: vendor post-up/comment/hwaddress lines preserved verbatim and in order, byte-identical second save (idempotency), unchanged output for a conf with no foreign lines, malformed/duplicate-stanza fallback to backup+regeneration, the 64-line/512-byte/control-char bounds, and the sibling rule (canonical always written, legacy mirrored as allow-hotplug only while live, retired once the device is gone). The merge is Bash inside a CGI, so no other row reaches it — a silent re-break of vendor-hook preservation would otherwise pass every syntax/static gate.
tools.init: bash (stdlib only, no deps) — run on demand: bash scripts/dev/test-iface-conf-merge.sh

tools.checks: Functional regression for the rename script's per-device udev-initialized gate (etc/sa02m-iface-canonical.sh canonicalize_pair, contract §1.0): settled-canonical immediate no-op, initialized-legacy rename, the boot-0 sequence (kernel-named eth0 that udev renames to end0 mid-wait — the 6.1-class 'board unreachable on an unattended boot' regression), absent-pair budget, both degraded-fallback branches (udev db never appears), and the failed-rename exit/admin-state discipline. Runs the SHIPPED functions against a sandboxed SYS_NET/UDEV_DB pair with an `ip` PATH shim — the systemd/udev timing it enumerates is unreachable from any other row and cannot be forced on a healthy bench board.
tools.init: bash (stdlib only, no deps) — run on demand: bash scripts/dev/test-iface-canonical-gate.sh

tools.checks: Regression for the installer's on-disk migration to canonical interface names (scripts/02-network.sh migrate_iface_conf): the three gate branches (canonical device live / explicit --ip protected / DUAL-CONF deferred), DUAL-CONF re-run idempotency incl. the canonical header NOT being demoted to allow-hotplug, a stanza-free legacy conf being dropped rather than copied over the live one, and eth1's allow-hotplug convention. This code only runs on a device as root during an install and its failure mode is 'the board comes up with no address' (the 1.0.3.38 Cannot-find-device class), so it gets a bench-runnable net.
tools.init: bash (stdlib only, no deps) — run on demand: bash scripts/dev/test-iface-migration.sh

tools.checks: Functional regression for the installer's gateway/DNS repair (scripts/02-network.sh ensure_gw_dns + the subnet helpers it uses from scripts/lib.sh): the mandatory subnet guard (an out-of-subnet candidate is NOT written — writing one makes the next ifup fail, networking.service FAILED, board unreachable: the 1.0.3.38 class through a new door), including via a CIDR `address a.b.c.d/NN` prefix and against a duplicated address/netmask key (two netmask lines were the one construction that got past the guard); fail-closed on any unparseable stanza with each branch asserted on its WARN TEXT, not just on 'nothing was written' (the install log is this code's only failure surface, so a message contradicting the file is itself the defect); add-only-when-absent (a present or deliberately commented-out gateway/dns-nameservers is never modified); no write into a dhcp or duplicate stanza; byte-identical re-runs with no backup churn; the .sa02m-gwbak name never clobbering the panel's .sa02m-bak restore point; insertion matching the stanza's own indent (four spaces / column 0 / TAB) without reordering hwaddress, post-up, comments or a preceding no-auto-down; and the write-failure contract — with mktemp/cp/mv stubbed to fail, and with a replace that lands the wrong content, the repair must log no OK, set no live-route flag, and leave or restore the conf (a false success would drive `ip route replace` plus a resolvconf head naming a gateway absent from the conf). Also covers sa02m_write_resolvconf_head: our stale head removed and logged, a foreign head never touched. The defect class is parsing and idempotency against real-world formatting variance, which a static grep gate cannot see — same reason iface-conf-merge and iface-migration exist. Non-vacuous: a failed or over-wide extraction, an un-retargeted conf path (which would edit the real /etc), a missing safety token in the extracted body, a missing lib.sh helper, or a fixture that stopped matching FAILS rather than passing on zero matches; the injection cases carry their own control assertion.
tools.init: bash (stdlib only, no deps) — run on demand: bash scripts/dev/test-iface-gw-repair.sh

tools.checks: Functional regression for the gateway-in-subnet validators in cgi-bin/lib_web_validate.sh (ipv4_to_int/netmask_is_contiguous/same_ipv4_subnet) and the apply.cgi empty-gateway guard: the customer bug (192.168.1.135/24 + gw 192.168.10.1 rejected), in-subnet /24 //16 //25 accepted, out-of-subnet rejected, non-contiguous/zero netmask rejected, leading-zero octet forced base-10 (010 read decimal, not octal), and both interfaces' `[ -n "$GATEWAY" ]` guards present so an empty gateway stays allowed. Pure-Bash math inside a CGI lib no other row reaches — a silent re-open of the dead-route footgun would otherwise pass every syntax/static gate.
tools.init: bash (stdlib only, no deps) — run on demand: bash scripts/dev/test-subnet-validate.sh

tools.checks: Regression for the donor-metadata handoff in tools/imaging/make-image.sh step 6 (collect_donor_metadata -> write_manifest): every field lands in its own manifest slot on a healthy donor whose /proc/device-tree/model is NUL-terminated with NO trailing newline (the field-shift class: a merged or absent line shifts every later field into the wrong slot), on a degraded donor (absent model file, conf without the profile key, failing dpkg-query), plus the donor-supplied serial_profile without the --profile override, a value containing '=', and a malformed DONOR_META. Extracts the SHIPPED collect_donor_metadata remote body and the SHIPPED write_manifest python (extraction anchored to their owning functions — the file carries other heredocs with the same tags) and runs them against a sandboxed fake donor: no ssh, no device, nothing touches the real system. Non-vacuous both ways: an empty or over-captured extraction FAILS, and MAKE_IMAGE_SRC pointed at a pre-fix script fails loudly (see the test header for the recipe).
tools.init: bash + Python 3 as python3/python/py (stdlib only, no deps) — run on demand: bash scripts/dev/test-image-manifest.sh

tools.checks: Byte-level regression for the U-Boot boot.scr generator (tools/imaging/uboot-script.py and its two producers). TWICE a malformed boot.scr shipped and the board stopped in U-Boot, because the only assertion was `grep -aq threadirqs`, which a malformed file passes. The byte layout it pins has ONE home — docs/contracts/uboot-boot-script.md; the golden is anchored to the donor facts recorded there, not to the writer's logic. Covers: the golden artifact, five malformed shapes rejected, the payload pins (size + LF + sha256, and the UNVERIFIED-ON-HARDWARE marker that stops a silent promotion), and the caller chain — it RUNS make-image.sh's shipped patch invocation against a sudo shim, so a step skipped because of a mode bit or a selector stripped by env_reset FAILS here rather than shipping a bad image. No mkimage, no device, no network — mkimage is a pipeline prereq but absent in CI. Non-vacuous both ways: an unresolvable writer or a missing guard/function FAILS, and BOOTSCR_SRC pointed at a pre-fix generator fails loudly (recipe in the test header).
tools.init: bash + Python 3 as python3/python/py (stdlib only, no deps) — run on demand: bash scripts/dev/test-uboot-bootscr.sh

tools.checks: Functional regression for the Node-RED install logic in etc/sa02m-web-service-ctl.sh — the code behind Управление → Службы → Node-RED, whose whole defect class is SILENT on the device. Runs the SHIPPED functions against a sandbox (payload resolution through the SA02M_NODERED_DIR seam, journalctl/sleep PATH shims, mutating helpers stubbed — nothing extracts a tarball, writes /usr/lib or talks to systemd): a half-staged directory is not a payload; the Node-tarball glob never selects node-red-*.tar.gz (that mis-selection extracted the Node-RED tree into /usr/local on a Node-less board and still failed); a cross-major overwrite is refused with both versions named and a next step in the log, while a clean install and a same-major update still proceed; the flow-level verdict, IN BOTH LOG LANGUAGES (node-red localises its runtime log: the bench board writes «Запущены потоки», so an English-only check silently stops firing there) — port 1880 open with the flows stopped is install_failed, NOT success; a unit that logged for the whole poll window without ever reporting started flows is a FAILURE rather than 'no evidence'; only a total absence of journal degrades to the honest runtime_only label; and the dispatch order (staged payload beats a reachable registry, no payload behaves exactly as before). Plus static wiring pins the behavioural cases cannot see: both install paths still CALL the major guard, and the offline path still stops the unit, removes the old tree before extracting (tar merges — it never deletes), and asserts a single node-red/ top level before a root extraction. Non-vacuous: a failed or short extraction FAILS rather than passing on zero matches.
tools.init: bash (stdlib only, no deps) — run on demand: bash scripts/dev/test-nodered-ctl.sh

tools.checks: Static gate for the Node-RED pin across its five homes — the runtime install (etc/sa02m-web-service-ctl.sh), the install-time path (scripts/07-nodered.sh), the payload build recipe (scripts/dev/build-nodered-payload.sh), the committed dependency manifest (vendor-src/nodered/package{,-lock}.json) and the documented payload shape (docs/vendor-integrations.md). Pins: one and only one node-red version string across all five (the lockfile is the ground truth — a constant that disagrees with the tree npm ci installs IS the drift); --node22 present in both install homes; NO surviving `node-red@3` / `--node20` anywhere under etc/ scripts/ tools/ (the EOL pin this row exists to keep out); --omit=optional and npm ci in the build recipe (dropping either reintroduces the native @node-rs/bcrypt dep and re-binds the payload to one Node ABI, or re-resolves ranges and ends reproducibility); the ctl's Node floor (major AND minor) mirroring engines.node of the pinned node-red in the lockfile, so a lockfile bump that raises the floor fails the build instead of leaving a board installing a runtime it cannot boot; the flow verdict surviving a non-English board (our unit pins LC_ALL, and BOTH readers match the en and ru spellings of the started-flows marker — plus neither may depend on 'Flows stopped due to missing node types', which is an editor-UI notification the runtime never logs, i.e. a check that cannot fire in any locale); and the repo-owned etc/systemd/system/nodered.service existing, running as User=nodered, and resolving node by ABSOLUTE path rather than env/PATH (a board can carry apt's Node beside a staged tarball Node — PATH order would otherwise decide which one runs). Non-vacuous: a missing file, an empty extraction, or a sweep that stops seeing files FAILS rather than passing on zero matches.
tools.init: bash + grep (present everywhere the project builds)

tools.checks: Functional regression for the RS-485 port-lease gate in etc/sa02m-web-service-ctl.sh (flasher_poll_lock_held -> cmd_list's `flasher_busy` field and cmd_start's mplc4/mqtt-bridge refusal). The gate was DEAD from 2026-07-12 to 2026-08-06 and no gate saw it: the probe sent a retired static session token and `curl -sS` WITHOUT `-f` exits 0 on the resulting 401, so the function answered 'not busy' forever while a flash held the line. Every symptom is silent — no syntax error, no failed unit, just Пуск buttons that stay enabled mid-flash. Runs the SHIPPED functions against a `curl` PATH shim that MODELS THE DAEMON'S AUTH RULE (hex session_token 32..128 authorized, anything else a real 401 with the body on stdout and exit 0; /health served regardless of cookie, as the daemon dispatches it above _check_auth) — a shim returning a fixed answer would pass before AND after the fix, so §0 asserts the shim's own rule first. Cases: a HELD lease reads BUSY (the assertion the original work never had — BUGLOG.md:1562 recorded only the IDLE observation, which is bit-identical to the broken state), idle reads not-busy, socket absent reads not-busy, and the whole fail-closed quadrant (timeout / HTTP 500 / non-JSON / valid JSON with no poll_locked i.e. an older daemon / empty body / curl absent) reads BUSY with the reason logged. Plus the JSON surface the panel actually consumes (cmd_list, cmd_start, and a control that docker is NOT gated) and static pins on the shipped file (-f present, no Cookie, /health, poll_locked, -S socket test, both call sites still wired, and /health still dispatched ABOVE the daemon's auth check). Non-vacuous: a failed extraction or a missed sandbox retarget FAILS rather than passing on zero matches; PORT_LEASE_SRC re-runs it against any older revision (recipe in the test header).
tools.init: bash (stdlib only, no deps) — run on demand: bash scripts/dev/test-port-lease-gate.sh

tools.checks: Static gate closing the dead-credential class repo-wide, so a sixth call site cannot appear. The fixed cookie `cyntron_session` was retired 2026-07-12 for a server-side session store (www/network_config/cgi-bin/lib_web_auth.sh — the one home of the auth rule) and five callers kept sending it for 3.5 weeks; a dead token is syntactically perfect, so no syntax/type/unit check can see it. Pins: (A) the CLASS — a `session_token=` whose value is a hard-coded word rather than an expansion, an empty logout value, a regex or a live-shaped hex token; (B) the retired string itself anywhere in etc/ www/ opt/ tools/ scripts/ install.sh; (C) non-vacuity BOTH ways — the roots exist and >=50 files are really swept, AND both allow-listed negative assertions are still present AND still negative. The allow-list is exactly two files that name the token in order to prove it is REFUSED: opt/sa02m-flasher/tests/test_auth.py (the rejected-token list inside test_non_hex_token_rejected, which must keep asserting False) and scripts/dev/test-port-lease-gate.sh (its shim's 401/-f control). Deleting either turns this gate RED, not green — and the pin-C check strips comments first, because the rejection test carries a COMMENT naming the token right above the assertion and accepting that as proof would stay green after the assertion was deleted. Deliberate non-flags: whole comment lines (the three scripts that used to send the token explain the defect in prose), empty values, expansions, regexes and prefix tests, and docs/ + CHANGELOG.md + .ai-dev/ which legitimately quote the token as history. Known limit, stated: only #- and //-comment lines are masked, so prose in a Python docstring must point at lib_web_auth.sh rather than spell the token.

tools.checks: Regression for the ES-module half of scripts/sync-app-version.py (scripts/dev/test_sync_app_version.py, stdlib unittest): a stale ?v= inside an import/export specifier (static from-imports, bare import, dynamic import(), both quote styles, multi-line bodies, an &r= suffix) is FLAGGED by --check and PATCHED by the sync; a ?v= that is not an import specifier (a runtime-built string, Array.from(...), a classic bundle) stays byte-identical; the shipped static/js tree is a byte-identical no-op; and main(['--check']) returns 1 with a stale module and 0 once synced. Without it the day the first module cluster lands, nginx's expires 1h could serve a stale imported module right after «Обновление веб» with version-consistency still green.
